population.span: Adult patients (aged 18–80 years) scheduled for elective on‐pump CABG were eligible.

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy outcome was the incidence of any documented episode of POAF (defined as AF lasting ≥30 s) within the first 14 days after surgery.

estimate.span: The primary outcome occurred in 14 patients (17.3%) in the colchicine group and 38 patients (46.3%) in the placebo group (Relative Risk [RR] 0.37, 95% CI 0.21–0.66; p < 0.001).

ci.span: The primary outcome occurred in 14 patients (17.3%) in the colchicine group and 38 patients (46.3%) in the placebo group (Relative Risk [RR] 0.37, 95% CI 0.21–0.66; p < 0.001).

analysis_set.span: The primary analysis was conducted using a modified intention‐to‐treat approach.

treatment_strategy.span: In this randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial, 172 adults scheduled for on‐pump CABG received colchicine or placebo. The regimen included a preoperative loading dose (1 mg twice daily) followed by a weight‐based maintenance dose (0.5 mg daily if <70 kg; 1 mg daily if ≥70 kg) for 14 days.

follow_up.span: The primary efficacy outcome was the incidence of any documented episode of POAF (defined as AF lasting ≥30 s) within the first 14 days after surgery.

served_mismatch: The served RR and CI match the source numerically, but their attribution to intention-to-treat and in-hospital/index-admission follow-up is incorrect. The source reports a modified intention-to-treat primary analysis and POAF within 14 days after surgery, including monitoring beyond hospitalization.
